about: Overview

Leaflegal is a free introduction service for people and businesses who need help from a lawyer. You tell us what is going on in a short form, and we introduce you to one regulated law firm that handles that kind of matter. For immigration, we introduce you to a regulated immigration adviser. The firm then gets in touch to talk it through with you.

Most people only need a solicitor a handful of times in their life. When the moment comes it is usually stressful, and it is hard to know where to start. A search brings up hundreds of names. Some firms only do certain kinds of work, some are not taking on new clients, and some are too far away or too expensive for what you need. You can lose a day ringing round and still not be sure you have found the right person.

Leaflegal takes away that first round of searching. You explain your situation once, in plain words. We read your answers, work out what kind of matter it is, and pass it to a firm that deals with that kind of work every day. The firm already knows the basics before it calls, so the first conversation can be about your situation rather than about whether they do this sort of thing at all.

about: The firm we introduce you to is a separate, independent business. It is regulated by its own professional body and it is responsible for the advice it gives you. We do not tell you what to do about your matter, and we do not see the advice the firm gives. Our part is to make the introduction carefully and to be honest with you about how it works.

Our users are a mix of homeowners, families, landlords, licensees and business owners. Some have a firm deadline, such as a court date or a completion date. Others are at the very start and just want to understand what happens next. Both are welcome. You do not need to know the legal name for your problem before you start. If you are not sure which area fits, choose the closest one or tell us in your own words and we will look at it.

Our pages explain in general terms how each kind of matter usually works, what it tends to cost and what to have ready. They are written to help you have a better conversation with a lawyer, not to replace one. Every situation is different, and the firm will look at the details of yours before telling you what your options are.
Using Leaflegal

The form takes about two minutes. It asks a few multiple choice questions about the kind of help you need, how urgent it is and where you are, followed by your name and contact details. There is space to add a short note in your own words if you want to.

about.h3: Step 1. Tell us what you need

about: Pick the area of law that is closest to your situation and answer the questions. Be as accurate as you can about dates, deadlines and the stage you have reached. If a court hearing is next week, or your buyer wants to exchange contracts soon, say so. It helps the firm judge how quickly to get in touch.

We check your enquiry and pass it to one regulated firm that handles your type of matter and covers your area. We do not send it to a list. That means you are not chased by several firms at once, and the firm that does call knows it is the only one you have been introduced to through us.

The firm usually gets in touch the same working day, often by phone. Enquiries made in the evening or at the weekend are usually picked up on the next working day. On that first call the firm will ask some questions, explain how it could help and tell you about its fees. You do not have to decide anything on the call.

If you want to go ahead, the firm will send you its terms of business and a written estimate or quote. It will also carry out its own identity checks, which regulated firms have to do before they act for a new client. If you do not want to go ahead, you can simply say so. There is no fee to pay us either way.

Sometimes a firm decides it cannot take on a matter once it understands the details. That might be because of a conflict of interest, because the matter needs a different kind of specialist, or because the firm is too busy to meet your deadline. When that happens the firm should tell you, so you can look elsewhere.

about: Areas we cover

Leaflegal covers seven areas of law. Five are for matters in England and Wales. The other two cover the whole of the UK. Trademarks and related IP are UK wide because there is one UK trademark register, and introductions to regulated immigration advisers are UK wide because immigration law is the same across the UK. You can read more about each area on its own page.

Within each area there are pages on the most common matters, such as buying a leasehold flat, a financial settlement on divorce or a premises licence application. If your matter is not listed, it may still be covered. Tell us what is happening and we will check.

Buying, selling or remortgaging a home or a buy to let property in England and Wales. This includes leasehold flats, new builds, transfers of equity and buying and selling at the same time. A conveyancer checks the title, runs searches, deals with the other side and registers the change of ownership.

Help for flat and house owners whose lease is getting shorter. That includes extending a lease under the statutory process, agreeing an informal extension with the freeholder and joining with neighbours to buy the freehold.

Divorce, dissolution of a civil partnership, financial settlements, consent orders, child arrangements, separation agreements, prenuptial agreements and disputes between people who lived together without marrying.
Premises licences for pubs, bars, restaurants, shops and venues. That covers new applications, variations, transfers, changes of designated premises supervisor and licence reviews.

Help for businesses that are owed money by other businesses, such as unpaid invoices. That includes letters before action, county court claims and statutory demands. We do not cover debts owed by individual consumers.

Introductions to a regulated immigration adviser, for individuals, families and employers anywhere in the UK. Leaflegal does not give immigration advice and does not tell you which visa or route might apply to you. The adviser we introduce will talk that through with you.

We do not handle personal injury, clinical negligence, housing disrepair or financial mis-selling claims. We also cannot help with matters that are only suitable for legal aid, or with debts owed to a business by private individuals. If your matter is outside our areas, organisations such as Citizens Advice and the Law Society's Find a Solicitor service can help you find the right kind of help.
Choosing a solicitor

Whether you use Leaflegal or find a firm another way, it helps to know what to look for. A good fit is not only about legal skill. It is also about how the firm communicates, how it charges and whether it has time for your matter.

Solicitors in England and Wales are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority, and you can look up a solicitor or firm on the SRA register. Licensed conveyancers are regulated by the Council for Licensed Conveyancers. Immigration advisers must be regulated too, either as solicitors or barristers or through the Immigration Advice Authority. Every firm we introduce is regulated, and it is still sensible to check for yourself.

Ask how often the firm handles matters like yours. A firm that does a lot of lease extensions or licence reviews will know the usual process and the usual pitfalls. You can ask who will do the work day to day and how much experience they have.

Some people want regular updates by phone. Others are happy with email and a call at key moments. Ask how the firm keeps clients informed and how quickly it usually replies. It is a fair question, and a good firm will be happy to answer it.

Before any work starts, a regulated firm should explain how it charges and confirm that in writing. That might be a fixed fee, an hourly rate with an estimate, or a mix of both. Ask what is included, what is not and what might make the cost go up.

For many matters, such as conveyancing or a lease extension, the firm does not need to be near you because most of the work is done by phone, email and post. For others, such as a hearing at a local magistrates' court or a licence application to your local council, local knowledge can be useful. We take your location into account when we make the introduction.

It is fine to take time to think after a first call. It is also fine to speak to more than one firm before you decide. Leaflegal introduces one firm, but there is no obligation to instruct them, and you remain free to look elsewhere.
Costs

Leaflegal is free to use. You do not pay us to fill in the form, to be introduced or at any later stage. We are paid by the firm we introduce you to, which pays us a fee for the introduction. That fee does not change what the firm charges you.
Solicitors must tell you in writing about any fee they pay for an introduction, and that fee must not affect the advice they give you. You can read more on our how we make money page.

The cost of legal help depends on the type of matter, how complex it is and the firm. Some kinds of work are often done for a fixed fee, such as many house purchases, uncontested divorces or straightforward licence applications. Others are usually charged by the hour because it is hard to know at the start how much work will be needed, such as a contested financial settlement or a defended court case.

Many firms ask for some money on account before they start, especially where there are disbursements to pay early on. Others bill at set stages or at the end. The firm will explain how its billing works in its terms of business.

On top of the firm's own fee there may be costs paid to other people. Examples include search fees and Land Registry fees on a property purchase, court fees on a claim, valuation fees on a lease extension or barristers' fees for a hearing. These are often called disbursements. They change from time to time, so the firm will tell you what applies to your matter and GOV.UK lists many official fees.

Privacy
We know that the details of a legal matter are personal. A separation, a driving charge or a debt can be hard to talk about, and you need to know where that information goes.

We share your details with one firm only, the firm we introduce you to, and only when you agree to that introduction on the form. We do not sell your details to lists of firms, and we never share the details of your matter with advertisers or data brokers.

We keep a record of your enquiry, the consent you gave and which firm we introduced you to. That lets us answer questions, deal with complaints and show that the introduction was made properly. Our privacy policy explains what we hold, how long we keep it and your rights, including how to ask for a copy or ask us to delete it.

about.h3: Once the firm has your details

about: The firm becomes responsible for how it uses your information. Regulated law firms have strict duties of confidentiality to their clients, and they also have their own data protection obligations. If you instruct the firm, what you tell them is treated as confidential in the usual way.
If you no longer want to hear from the firm, you can tell them directly. You can also contact us and we will let them know. Changing your mind does not cost you anything.
faqs: About Leaflegal
What is Leaflegal?

Leaflegal is a free introduction service. You tell us about your legal matter in a short form and we introduce you to one regulated law firm that handles that kind of work, or for immigration, a regulated adviser. The firm then contacts you to talk it through. Leaflegal is a trading name of Vertical Brands Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales.
Is Leaflegal a law firm?

No. We are an introduction service. We are not a law firm, we are not regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority and we do not give legal advice or immigration advice. The firm we introduce you to is independent and regulated, and its lawyers are responsible for the advice they give you.
Why use Leaflegal instead of searching myself?

You can always search yourself. Leaflegal saves you the first round of phone calls by passing your enquiry to a firm that already handles your type of matter and covers your area. The firm knows the basics before it calls, so the first conversation tends to be more useful. You are still free to compare and choose.
Who runs Leaflegal?

Leaflegal is run by Vertical Brands Ltd, registered in England and Wales with company number 14254961. You can find our full company details on our about page. If you have a question about how we work, you can email us and we will reply as soon as we can.
Can businesses use Leaflegal?

Yes. Businesses use Leaflegal for debt recovery from other businesses, premises licences, sponsor licences and other employer immigration matters, and for buying and selling property. The form asks whether you are enquiring as a person or a business, so we can introduce a firm that deals with that kind of client.
Do you cover Scotland and Northern Ireland?

For most areas, no. Conveyancing, family law, licensing, lease extensions and debt recovery are covered for England and Wales only, because Scotland and Northern Ireland have separate legal systems. Immigration introductions are available across the whole of the UK.
The introduction
How long does the form take?

About two minutes for most people. You answer a few multiple choice questions about the type of matter, how urgent it is and where you are, then give your name and contact details. You can add a short note in your own words if there is something important the firm should know before it calls.
How quickly will a firm contact me?

Usually the same working day, and often within a few hours during office hours. Enquiries made in the evening, at the weekend or on a bank holiday are usually picked up on the next working day. If your matter is very urgent, say so in the form so the firm knows to prioritise it.
How many firms will contact me?

One. We introduce each enquiry to a single regulated firm, never to a list. That means you will not be chased by several firms at once. If you want a second opinion or another quote, you are free to contact other firms yourself at any point.
How do you choose the firm?

We look at the type of matter, where you are and any details you give us, and introduce you to a regulated firm that handles that kind of work and covers your area. We do not choose firms based on who pays us most, and we do not recommend one outcome over another.
Do I have to instruct the firm?

No. There is no obligation at any stage. You can listen to what the firm says, ask questions, take time to think and then decide. If you decide not to go ahead, just tell the firm. You will not owe Leaflegal anything whatever you decide.
What if the firm cannot help me?

Sometimes a firm decides it cannot take on a matter once it understands the details, for example because of a conflict of interest or a tight deadline it cannot meet. The firm should tell you if that happens. You are then free to look for another firm, and organisations such as the Law Society can help.
What if I miss the firm's call?

Firms usually try more than once and may also send an email or a text. Check your voicemail and junk folder. If you have not heard anything by the end of the next working day, contact us and we will look into it for you.
Can I use Leaflegal for more than one matter?

Yes. If you have two separate matters, such as selling a house and a driving charge, you can fill in the form for each one. Each enquiry is introduced to a firm that handles that type of work, so you may hear from a different firm for each. Mention any link between them in the notes.
Costs and fees
Does it cost anything to use Leaflegal?

No. Leaflegal is free to use. You do not pay us for the form, the introduction or anything afterwards. We are paid a fee by the firm we introduce you to. That fee does not change what the firm charges you, and the firm must tell you about it in writing.
How much will the solicitor charge?

That depends on the type of matter, how complex it is and the firm. Some work is usually done for a fixed fee and some is charged by the hour. The firm will explain its fees on the first call and confirm them in writing before any work starts, so you know where you stand.
What are disbursements?

Disbursements are costs the firm pays to other people on your behalf, such as court fees, search fees, Land Registry fees or a barrister's fee. They are usually listed separately from the firm's own fee. Many official fees change from time to time, so ask the firm for an up to date breakdown.
Why does the firm pay you?

That is how Leaflegal is funded. Firms pay us for introductions because it saves them the cost of finding clients in other ways. It means we can keep the service free for you. You can read exactly how it works on our how we make money page.
Can I get legal aid through Leaflegal?

No. We introduce people who are looking for paid legal help. Legal aid is only available for certain matters and depends on your circumstances. If you think you might qualify, use the legal aid checker on GOV.UK, which can point you to a provider that does legal aid work.
Is the fee the firm pays you added to my bill?

No. The fee the firm pays us for the introduction does not change what the firm charges you. The firm sets its own prices and will explain them to you before you agree to anything. Solicitors must also tell you about the introduction fee in writing so that everything is open.
Your details
Who do you share my details with?

Only the one firm we introduce you to, and only if you agree on the form. We do not sell your details to lists of firms, and we never share the details of your matter with advertisers or data brokers. Our privacy policy explains this in full.
Is what I tell you confidential?

We treat your enquiry as private and only share it with the firm we introduce. Once you instruct a regulated firm, its lawyers owe you a duty of confidentiality. Leaflegal is not a law firm, so the legal protections that apply to conversations with your lawyer do not apply to the form itself.
Can I ask you to delete my details?

Yes. You can ask us for a copy of the information we hold about you or ask us to delete it. Some records may need to be kept for a period, for example to show that your consent was given. Our privacy policy explains your rights and how to use them.
Will I get marketing messages?

We use your details to make the introduction you asked for. We do not pass the details of your matter to advertisers. If we ever want to send you anything else, we will only do so in line with our privacy policy and the choices you have made.
What if I no longer want to hear from the firm?
Tell the firm directly that you do not want to go ahead. You can also contact us and we will pass the message on. Changing your mind costs you nothing and there is no need to give a reason.
Getting help
I am not sure which area my problem falls under

That is fine. Choose the closest option on the form, or tell us in your own words what is happening. Many problems touch more than one area, such as a separation that involves selling a house. The firm will explain which kind of help fits once it understands your situation.
Do you give legal advice?

No. Leaflegal does not give legal advice or immigration advice, and nothing on this website is advice about your situation. Our pages explain how things usually work in general terms. A solicitor or regulated adviser will look at your own circumstances and tell you what your options are.
Can you help with personal injury claims?

No. Leaflegal does not cover personal injury, clinical negligence, housing disrepair or financial mis-selling claims. If you need help with one of these, the Law Society's Find a Solicitor service lists firms that do that kind of work, and Citizens Advice can explain where to start.
How do I complain about Leaflegal?

Email us with the word complaint in the subject line, telling us what went wrong and what you would like us to do. We acknowledge complaints within three working days and aim to give a full written reply within fifteen working days. Our complaints page has the details.
How do I complain about the firm?

Raise it with the firm first. Every regulated firm must have a complaints procedure. If the firm does not resolve a complaint about its service within eight weeks, you may be able to go to the Legal Ombudsman. Please tell us too, because we take how firms treat people seriously.
What should I have ready before the call?

Anything that explains your matter, such as letters, contracts, court papers, a memorandum of sale or invoices. A photo on your phone is fine at first. It also helps to note key dates and deadlines and a few questions about fees, timescales and who will handle your matter day to day.
Can I fill in the form for someone else?

You can make an enquiry on behalf of a family member or a business you work for, as long as they are happy for you to do so. The firm will usually need to speak to the person or business it is acting for directly, and it will need to carry out its own identity checks before taking instructions.
